newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors to call ex-minister in arms scam probe.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors to call ex-minister in arms scam probe.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors will summon a former defence minister in connection with an arms scandal, prosecution officials said on Thursday.
"The prosecution has decided to summon Mr Lee Yang-ho in connection with the arms scandal. He will be summoned soon, possibly later today," one official said.

President Kim Young-sam ordered an investigation into the scandal last week after the main opposition party, the National Congress for New Politics, claimed that Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd paid 300 million won ($362,000) in bribes to an arms dealer last year to arrange a government purchase of military helicopters.
Daewoo admitted giving money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe. Lee, who has denied accusations of wrongdoing, was sacked by Kim last week.
Another prosecution official said Sok Chin-chol, who was the president of Daewoo Heavy last year, was being questioned on Thursday in connection with the kickback probe.
On Wednesday night prosecutors also grilled Daewoo Group Chairman Yoon Young-suk and Chung Ho-shin, vice president of Daewoo Heavy, a group unit.
